title: Illuminating the dark kinome utilizing multiplex peptide activity arrays to functionally annotate understudied kinases

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract ("195 novel kinase-substrate interactions") vs. Results (peptide counts per kinase)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Results report 18 high + 31 medium + 4 low = 53 peptides for EPHA6, and 26/31/6 (TNK1) = 63, 9/46/10 (AATK) = 65, 3/4/8 (INSRR) = 15, 3/1/1 (LTK) = 5, totaling 201 kinase-peptide interactions, not the 195 claimed in the Abstract. The number also cannot be an 'unique peptide' count, since the chip only carries 193 reporter peptides (195 > 193).

"schizophrenia (16, M:8 and F:9) subjects" — 8 males plus 9 females equals 17, not 16. The sex breakdown contradicts the stated group size (the control group, 17 with M:8/F:9, is internally consistent), so one of the two numbers is wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, recombinant kinase constructs (AATK E1216-A1374; INSRR L24-A747; LTK S20-P424)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated amino-acid ranges do not contain the catalytic kinase domains of these proteins: human AATK (1374 aa) has its kinase domain at ~aa 131–391, so E1216–A1374 is the C-terminal tail; human INSRR (1297 aa) has its kinase domain at ~aa 1013–1286, so L24–A747 is the extracellular ectodomain; human LTK (864 aa) has its kinase domain at ~aa 510–778, so S20–P424 is the extracellular domain. Fragments lacking the catalytic domain cannot phosphorylate reporter peptides, yet AATK is reported to give the highest chip coverage (34%), contradicting the premise that these screens measure intrinsic kinase activity.

"The default settings of the standard STK analysis protocol were used with the additional step of upstream kinase analysis" — all arrays described in the paper are phospho-tyrosine (PTK) PamChips (catalog 86402, 193 PTK reporter peptides). Applying the serine/threonine (STK) analysis protocol/peptide-kinase mapping to PTK chip data is internally inconsistent and would yield invalid upstream kinase assignments.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, definition of 'dark' kinases; Results, normalized ranks
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Dark kinases are defined as "the bottom third percentile of the kinome ranked by standardized log-transformed INDRA statements," but the five selected kinases are stated to have "normalized ranks … from 0.20 to 0.28" (i.e., 20th–28th percentile), and 19 dark tyrosine kinases alone are said to be identified. With >500 human kinases, the bottom 3rd percentile would contain ~15 kinases in total, so the stated cutoff is incompatible with both the number of dark tyrosine kinases and the reported rank values (the intended criterion is evidently the bottom third, ~33rd percentile).

Fig. 2C is cited for two different data types: first for concentration–response signal intensity ("Signal intensity of phosphosites with increasing total protein (2.5 ng – 25 ng) … (Fig. 2C, Supplementary Fig. 2D, 2J, 2P, 2V)") and later for amino-acid sequence logos ("We visualized the amino acid sequence logos … (Fig. 2C, Supplementary Fig. 2E, 2K, 2Q, 2W)"). One of these panel references must be wrong; the main-figure panel lettering is inconsistent with the supplementary panel series.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, supplementary panel citations for pathway analysis
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Supplementary Fig. 2Q is cited both for sequence logos ("Supplementary Fig. 2E, 2K, 2Q, 2W") and for pathway analyses ("Fig. 2D, Supplementary Fig. 2F, 2L, 2Q, 2X"). Given the regular six-panel-per-kinase layout (A–F, G–L, M–R, S–X), the pathway citation should be 2R; the same panel cannot show both sequence logos and GO pathways.

The figure panel labels the 27%-coverage kinase as "EPHA8", whereas the caption and all text refer to EPHA6 (one of the five profiled dark kinases). EPHA8 is a different kinase and was never screened; the label contradicts the caption and the Results text.

"samples were spun down at 13×G for 15 min at 4°C" — a 13 × g spin cannot pellet cellular debris from brain homogenate; the standard condition is ~13,000 × g. As written, the separation of supernatant and pellet fractions described immediately afterwards would not be achievable.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract/Introduction claim of exploring AD and MDD
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract and Introduction state that the roles of the five dark kinases were explored in "schizophrenia, Alzheimer's dementia (AD), and major depressive disorder (MDD)", but the Methods describe only postmortem DLPFC from non-psychiatric control and schizophrenia subjects, and all presented analyses (kinome deconvolution, peptide set enrichment, EPHA6 network) concern schizophrenia only. No AD or MDD dataset or analysis is specified.
